question: Shared: prediction of MCI-to-AD conversion (conversion by month 36) in ADNI MCI, with MRI as the shared channel. P-199 (Lu et al., 2022) uses one baseline T1 image (3D ResNet-50, Med3D + MoCo). P-186 (Minhas et al., 2021) uses a linear SVM on three-visit trajectories of neuropsychological measures and FreeSurfer MRI features, with the last value forecast. Feature set, input timepoints, sample and validation differ, which condition 1 allows.

figures.P-199: AUC 0.835 on a held-out 20% test set, no AUC interval printed. Test class sizes from sensitivity 0.786 = 44/56 and specificity 0.850 = 51/60: 56 pMCI/60 sMCI. Hanley-McNeil: Q1 = 0.7167, Q2 = 0.7599, SE = 0.0382, 95% CI [0.760, 0.910].

matched_figure_check: A matched figure exists and reconciles the pair. P-186 reports MRI-only models, the channel P-199 uses: 0.905 (1-year-ahead) and 0.88 (6-month-ahead). P-199's 0.835 lies inside both intervals ([0.833, 0.977] by 0.002; [0.813, 0.947] clearly), and both P-186 MRI-only figures lie inside P-199's interval [0.760, 0.910]. The matched figures therefore agree in both directions at both horizons, although the 1-year margin is narrow. On the headline figures the gap is beyond uncertainty (0.957 is above P-199's upper bound 0.910; 0.835 is below P-186's lower bound 0.908). P-186 itself attributes its peak AUC to adding neuropsychological measures and the forecast conversion-time value.
performance_validity: Exclusion does not apply: 0.957 is below 0.97 (P-186's 'GT AUC' 0.98 is a ground-truth benchmark that uses observed future values, not a prediction). P-186 scales features before the train-test split and picks the subset size from results, which makes its figures optimistic, but that is not the Section 3.5 exclusion.
reason: The headline AUCs (0.835 vs 0.957) differ beyond uncertainty. But P-186's own MRI-only figures (0.905 and 0.88) agree with P-199's image-only 0.835 in both directions. The gap sits in P-186's added neuropsychological measures and forecast value, which P-186 reports, so condition 3 fails. The 1-year MRI-only interval contains 0.835 by only 0.002, so the reconciliation holds on the rule's arithmetic with little room.

quotes.quote: To prevent data leakage, only participants' baseline data were selected in this study.
ResNet-50 achieved the best performance with an accuracy of 0.819 and an AUC of 0.835
for 1-year-ahead prediction, the dataset contains three consecutive annual readings, resulting in 35 MCIp and 50 MCIs subjects.
i.e., 36th month, are called MCI progressors (MCIp), and those retaining MCI diagnosis at all times are known as MCI stables (MCIs).
MRI measures, despite being accurately forecasted, deliver the least classification AUC.

The method proposed in this paper has recorded the highest classification AUC of 95.7% predominantly because of involving the forecasted marker value at the time of conversion as a classification feature.
We scale all features to have values between 0 and 1 before the train-test split.
